note: Verified archival excerpts. Presidents are not asserted to be in office in the encounter year. Words are excerpts from the linked institutional records, not newly authored dialogue. Reuse the campus record by key rather than duplicating its quotation text.

penn.text: But I also believe that universities have a responsibility to use knowledge to serve humanity.
penn.author: Amy Gutmann
penn.sourceTitle: Inaugural Address, October 15, 2004 — archived Office of the President
penn.context: Archival excerpt from Gutmann’s 2004 inaugural address on a university’s public responsibility. It is not a statement made during the game’s 1896–97 visit.

harvard.text: We would have them all, and at their best.
harvard.author: Charles William Eliot
harvard.sourceTitle: Neil L. Rudenstine, Pointing Our Thoughts (2001), The Values of Education, printed page 5
harvard.context: Eliot’s 1869 inaugural words about embracing literary and scientific fields, quoted in an official Harvard presidential volume. This archival excerpt is separate from the fictional encounter dialogue.

indiana.text: Truly, the sun never sets on the work of a great university.
indiana.author: Herman B Wells
indiana.sourceTitle: IU President Michael A. McRobbie, Indianapolis Rotary Club remarks, February 23, 2016, page 14, footnote 1
indiana.context: The institutional transcript explicitly identifies this as Wells’s original wording from his Report on the State of the University, October 6, 1959, distinguishing it from McRobbie’s later paraphrase. Archival excerpt, not a 1990 meeting.

ucla.text: To expand the boundaries of our knowledge is simply one of our obligations to a civilization based on reason.
ucla.author: Clark Kerr
ucla.sourceTitle: The Worth of Intellect: Inaugural Address, September 29, 1958 — UC History Digital Archive, Bancroft Library
ucla.context: Archival excerpt from Kerr’s 1958 systemwide inaugural address, delivered at Berkeley. UCLA belongs to that system; Kerr is not being described as UCLA’s campus chancellor or as its 1995 leader.

notre-dame.text: Our words are buttressed by our deeds, and our deeds are inspired by our convictions.
notre-dame.author: Theodore M. Hesburgh, C.S.C.
notre-dame.sourceTitle: Hesburgh Quotes — university memorial site, citing Contemporary Issues in Higher Education (1985)
notre-dame.context: An archival 1985 statement reproduced on Notre Dame’s official memorial site. It is not newly scripted advice or a claim that Hesburgh remained president in 1999.

columbia.text: It deals with real problems and it relates itself to life as it is.
columbia.author: Nicholas Murray Butler
columbia.sourceTitle: Lee C. Bollinger, Universities Must Think Globally, November 14, 2003 — Office of the President
columbia.context: Butler’s early-presidency description of the modern research university, quoted in Bollinger’s official 2003 essay. The archival statement is separate from the invented 2006 teaching scene.
